headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Goose can write/egress broadly while Rasa can relay dialogue to external channels, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, while Rasa can ingest and emit conversational text through external channels. A shared workspace or copied content can let attacker-controlled text from one agent influence the other, though no direct bridge is documented. Uncertainty about the exact integration path pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Goose and Rasa exchange content through a shared file, queue, or copied transcript
IF Rasa forwards untrusted user text into Goose prompts or MCP inputs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and disable shared folders
Require explicit human review before copying agent outputs between systems
Prefix imported text as untrusted data in prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, has broad network egress, and handles model-provider and extension tokens; Rasa handles text/voice and can send messages via multiple chat APIs. If either agent processes the same sensitive workspace, data can flow out through Goose's egress or Rasa's channels. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Goose's cwd
IF Rasa is connected to any external messaging channel listed in its profile
IF either agent is given the same customer data set
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of the shared workspace
Rotate or scope tokens before running Goose
Restrict Rasa channels to a test tenant
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, and supports multiple instances via filesystem sharing; Rasa does not support multiple instances and may also mutate conversation state through external channels. Concurrent writes or state updates can collide, and Goose's default self-isolation is none. Because the shared mutable surface is explicit and defaults are unsafe, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Goose instances operate on the same directory or git repo
IF Rasa and Goose write to a shared mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate checkout
Serialize git and file writes with a lock
Disable concurrent Goose sessions on the same workspace
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code or operational actions, and Rasa can surface text to users or downstream channels. If Rasa treats Goose output as authoritative without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect replies or actions. The pairwise pathway exists but is not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Rasa consumes Goose-produced text as a final answer or action plan
IF Goose output is forwarded into Rasa without a verification step
mitigations: Add a human review step before Rasa sends Goose-derived content
Require citations or structured schemas for Goose outputs
Log and diff Goose outputs before reuse
requires-engineering: implement automated fact-checking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Goose is an on-machine coding agent that touches source code and files in cwd, while Rasa handles text/voice and can transmit data through third-party messaging APIs. If regulated customer data is routed from Goose's workspace into Rasa channels, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated data from Goose's workspace is sent into any Rasa channel
IF the deployment uses a retention or residency policy different from the source data's requirements
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents' shared inputs
Use a non-production Rasa tenant for testing
Document retention settings for each channel
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and deletion controls
